newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Air eyes revenue from hotels.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Air eyes revenue from hotels.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said on Thursday that it was moving into hotel development to boost group revenue.
MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli said the company is reviving its dormant wholly-owned subsidiary, MAS Hotels & Boutiques Sdn Bhd, to look into developing and possibly acquiring hotels.

"We see that there is a lot of need for that division to be activated and we probably would have to invest (in hotels) in places that (MAS) is taking us," Tajudin told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
MAS, which operates national airline Malaysia Airlines, on Friday will launch its development of a five-star hotel in the northern Malaysian resort island of Langkawi.
Tajudin said MAS was also looking at building or acquiring hotels abroad to help house its flight staff, as well as a means to retain customer revenues.
He indicated MAS may be building a hotel near the new Kuala Lumpur airport at Sepang, located outside the capital city.
"We find that there are not going to be enough hotels (around Sepang) initially, so we have to undertake on our own," Tajudin said.
